hero.headline:
Gluten-free life,
told exactly as it is.
hero.body: Mother. Programmer. And for a few years now, an involuntary expert in reading labels. Here I talk about coeliac disease with no jargon and no sugar-coating — with just the right mix of useful and fed up that comes from asking "does this contain traces?" in every single restaurant.

about.title: From programmer to accidental advocate.
about.body: I was diagnosed with coeliac disease in 2018 and found out nobody explains what living with it is actually like: the packed lunch at every plan, the interrogation over every menu, and that feeling of being "the difficult one" in the group. I started posting about it on Instagram with humour because, if I don't laugh, nobody does.

meta.title: About me
meta.description: I'm Marta. Coeliac, mother and programmer, in that order depending on the day. Diagnosed in 2018, this is what I learned along the way.

hero.headline: I'm Marta. Coeliac, mother and programmer, in that order depending on the day.
hero.body: Diagnosed in 2018, overnight I went from eating whatever I fancied to reading labels like they were a new language. This is what I learned along the way — and what I'm still learning.

timeline.text: Coeliac diagnosis. The start of a crash course in "reading the small print on everything".
I start posting on Instagram what nobody talks about: the lunchbox in my backpack, the interrogation at every bar, and the funny side that's also in all of this.
@glutenfreemarta grows with reels, practical guides and a community that's just as fed up but laughs along with me. And now, with CeroGluten Lab, taking all of this one step further.

tone.title: Why the sarcastic tone?
tone.body: Because real coeliac disease isn't just "eating healthy". It's explaining for the hundredth time what a trace is, it's not being able to improvise a plan, it's sometimes feeling like the awkward one at the table. I'd rather laugh at that than let it define me. You won't find medical jargon here — that's what your doctor is for — but what living gluten-free is actually like.
